newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Sustained shelling shatters Brazzaville truce.
newsitem.headline: Sustained shelling shatters Brazzaville truce.

text.p: Sustained shelling and shooting shattered a fragile truce in the Congo Republic capital Brazzaville on Wednesday, witnesses across the river in Kinshasa reported.

It was not immediately clear whether supporters of President Pascal Lissouba or those of his predecessor, former military leader Denis Sassou Nguesso, had started the firing, which continued for at least half an hour.

Brazzaville residents and aid workers said earlier that the truce that began at midnight on Monday and was initialled by the two rivals had been "more or less respected" despite the occasional "very, very sporadic" burst of shooting.
Of numerous ceasefires declared since the bloody showdown between Lissouba and Sassou started on June 5, not one has been strictly adhered to.

Mohamed Sahnoun, the U.N. and Organisation for African Unity special envoy who met both sides in Brazzaville on Tuesday, said afterwards representatives of both sides might meet in Gabon's capital Libreville late Thursday or early Friday.
The showdown, in which hundreds of people have died, began after soldiers surrounded Sassou's home as part of a crackdown on private militias ahead of a now postponed July 27 presidential election.
